endorsements.quote: Clinicians must ensure that their use of AI in clinical decision-making is transparent and that patients receive adequate explanations of the decisions made by the AI system.

we should envision AI as a powerful ally to augment and support clinicians rather than a replacement, fostering a synergistic relationship between technology and human expertise to improve healthcare delivery and patient well-being.
Clinicians must remain critical and maintain due scrutiny to identify where the AI tool is flawed or makes incorrect predictions [ 14 ].

unlisted_practices: Conduct ongoing real-world evaluation of clinical AI to confirm that promise from pre-clinical data is borne out in practice.
Clinicians should develop the skills needed to steward the adoption of AI tools safely and effectively.

screen.reason: This is a reflective case report and perspective commentary discussing how AI decision support might help mitigate clinician cognitive bias, while highlighting potential pitfalls, governance, and training needs.
